stories.title: Yankees Birthday of the Day: Hugh High
stories.summary: Remembering a Yankees outfielder from the dawn of the franchise. Determined not to lose his New York franchise, AL president Ban Johnson worked behind the scenes during the 1914-15 offseason to strengthen the team's roster, making it more attractive for a prospective new ownership group. He did so by encouraging the rest of the league's teams to sell the Yankees useful players at a reasonable price. The first team to heed his call was the Tigers, who sold New York two players: a first-base prospect named Wally Pipp and a 27-year-old outfielder named Hugh High.

After their second-ever game in 1977, the matchup took a 12-year hiatus before resuming in 1989. It has been played on a more regular basis since then.
